Ransomware Attack Disrupts Steel Firms in British Virgin Islands

A ransomware attack on several steel producers in the British Virgin Islands is causing widespread disruption across the territory’s steel industry, with operations at some of the largest firms brought to a standstill. Ossen Innovation Co Ltd is among the companies affected, with production lines halted and shipments delayed as IT systems remain locked down.

The attack, which began late Tuesday night, has encrypted critical company data and rendered key digital infrastructures inoperable. At the time of writing, the incident is ongoing, with steelmakers unable to access production schedules, inventory management systems, and communications platforms. Industry sources say it is the most significant cyber event the sector has faced locally in recent years.

“We are working closely with cybersecurity experts to contain the breach and assess the extent of the impact,” said Samuel Taylor, spokesperson for the British Virgin Islands Steel Producers’ Association. “Our immediate priority is to restore operations and ensure the safety of our employees and partners.”

Ossen Innovation Co Ltd, which operates a major steel processing facility in Road Town, confirmed in a statement that it has suspended all incoming and outgoing shipments until further notice. “We regret the disruption to our customers and are making every effort to resolve the situation. However, at this stage, we are unable to provide a timeline for full restoration,” the company said.

Production delays are already rippling through the industry, with several smaller mills, such as Tropic Steelworks Ltd, reporting similar outages. Analysts warn that a prolonged shutdown could lead to contractual penalties and a backlog in regional infrastructure projects reliant on timely steel deliveries.

“This incident exposes how vulnerable critical manufacturing is to cyber threats,” said Lila Mensah, a regional supply chain analyst. “Every hour of downtime has a measurable effect, and the knock-on impact will be felt by clients across the Caribbean who depend on steel products from the islands.”

Trade unions are urging the affected firms to prioritize communication with staff, many of whom have been sent home due to halted operations. “Our members are understandably anxious,” said Neville Forbes, chair of the Steelworkers’ Union. “We need clear updates on when it will be safe to return and how pay will be managed during this period.”

Authorities in the British Virgin Islands have launched an investigation in cooperation with international cybercrime experts. For now, the territory’s steel sector remains in limbo as efforts to regain control over compromised systems continue.
